title_en: New Slang, New Stories (9/20): Talking About "Run-ology" After a Late Night at Work
note_en: 与其……不如…… means "rather than A, it's better to B": 与其天天纠结"润不润"，不如把每一天过扎实 "rather than agonizing every day over whether to 'run,' it's better to live each day well." The option you reject comes after 与其 and the better choice after 不如, much like English "rather than ..., better to ..." but more formal.

sentences.en: The coworker added that the word suddenly took off around 2022, when Shanghai was under a long COVID lockdown. Many people, stuck at home in quarantine, were searching online for "how to emigrate" and "how to go abroad," and that's how "run" came to be used so widely and gradually became a popular expression.
